fixedAssumptions.foodWasteSource: Netherlands Nutrition Centre (Voedingscentrum), 2026 report using 2025 data

householdCopy.wasteLabel: Food a household your size throws away
householdCopy.wasteInfo: Dutch average from the Netherlands Nutrition Centre (2026), about €100 per person a year. Your household may waste more or less.
householdCopy.offloadRateLabel: Share of planning time KAI takes on
householdCopy.foodWasteReferenceLabel: Food wasted per person each year
householdCopy.timeBackFormula: Time back = sessions × planning minutes per session × the share KAI takes on, minus sessions × minutes to check each plan.
householdCopy.wasteFormula: Food-waste comparison = food wasted per person each year ÷ 12 × people in your household, rounded to whole euros.
householdCopy.priceNote: The KAI price is fixed. None of these inputs change it.

copy.methodBody: KAI takes on part of the planning work: checking what is already at home, choosing recipes and preparing the list. Checking each plan still takes some of your time, so it is subtracted. The food-waste figure is a published average shown beside the KAI price for comparison, not a promised saving.
copy.noCurrencyChange: Language changes formatting, not your currency or assumptions.
copy.reviewError: Checking takes longer than the planning time KAI takes on. At these values there is no time back.

copy.brand.ariaLabel: KAI Retail: Inventory and Vendor Ordering
copy.brand.subtitle: Inventory & Vendor Ordering
copy.hero.eyebrow: KAI RETAIL · STOCK ACCURACY & VENDOR ORDERS
copy.hero.heading: Turn stock photos, counts and invoices into vendor-ready orders.
copy.hero.body: For multi-location grocery and specialty operators who still rely on spreadsheets and floor time. Your named approver reviews every suggested order.
copy.stage.captureHint: Tap to run the sample stock check
copy.stage.lastReconciled: Last physical count reconciled with the live list
copy.stage.billingNote: You keep direct vendor billing. KAI prepares the quantities and order format.
copy.pain.heading: Three lines an owner or operations lead knows too well.
copy.media.inventoryCountAlt: A grocery operations lead carrying out a physical stock count in a store room
copy.pain.mediaCaption: Start with a physical count your team can trust.
copy.media.painStockSpreadsheetAlt: An operations lead checking shelf stock against a laptop spreadsheet in a grocery stockroom
copy.pain.card1.heading: Stock counted in a spreadsheet that’s already wrong.
copy.pain.card1.body: The count was accurate when someone typed it. Sales, damaged stock, and new deliveries changed it immediately.
copy.media.painVendorLateAlt: A grocery buyer checking a phone beside fresh produce while facing a late replenishment gap
copy.pain.card2.heading: Vendor orders placed too late.
copy.pain.card2.body: The shelf gap is visible only after the order cut-off passes, turning a normal replenishment into an emergency.
copy.media.painMultiShopAlt: A multi-store buyer juggling phone calls, invoices, and a laptop at a grocery counter
copy.pain.card3.heading: One person covering several shops.
copy.pain.card3.body: The same buyer is checking messages, invoices, pack sizes, and stock notes across locations without one current view.
copy.loop.heading: Capture what is there. Order what is about to be missing.
copy.loop.body: A practical loop for the people already responsible for the shelf, not another system to maintain.
copy.loop.step1.heading: Capture stock from photos, invoices, or a simple list.
copy.loop.step1.body: A back-room photo, supplier invoice, or quick count is enough to update the working inventory.
copy.loop.step2.heading: KAI tracks on-hand, incoming, and likely run-out.
copy.loop.step2.body: Each SKU stays tied to current stock, incoming deliveries, and its recent pace of movement.
copy.loop.step3.heading: You approve a vendor order.
copy.loop.step3.body: KAI drafts the quantities against pack sizes and vendor minimums. One named approver decides what is placed.
copy.loop.step4.heading: You keep your vendors.
copy.loop.step4.body: KAI does not replace your ERP on day one. It starts as the operational layer between the physical count and the order.
copy.pilot.heading: Prove the stock loop in one place before you widen it.
copy.pilot.body: Choose one location or one category. Your staff uses KAI in the real operating rhythm, and one named approver reviews each suggested order.
copy.media.vendorOrderAlt: An independent grocery buyer reviewing a vendor order beside incoming produce
copy.pilot.guaranteeHeading: Inventory matches a physical count within an agreed error band, or the week is free.
copy.pilot.bullet4: Your existing vendors stay in place
copy.pilot.boundaryBody: We do not guarantee sell-through or supplier prices. The pilot measures stock accuracy and the cleanliness of vendor orders.
copy.scope.heading: Who KAI Retail is not for.
copy.media.vendorDeliveryAlt: Retail staff receiving grocery stock from an existing delivery partner
copy.scope.mediaCaption: Your vendors stay in place. KAI makes the handoff cleaner.
copy.media.homeCookAlt: A home cook preparing dinner in a domestic kitchen
copy.scope.card1.heading: Home cooks
copy.scope.card1.body: KAI Retail is for stores, wholesale teams, and the people responsible for stock.
copy.media.mealPlanningAlt: A person planning household meals at a kitchen table
copy.scope.card2.heading: Meal planning
copy.scope.card2.body: No recipes, cooking plans, or consumer meal suggestions appear in the retail workspace.
copy.media.consumerDeliveryAlt: A grocery courier delivering bags to a customer at home
copy.scope.card3.heading: Consumer grocery delivery
copy.scope.card3.body: This page is about replenishing shops and downstream retailers through existing vendors.
copy.form.heading: Start with the operation you most want to make reliable.
copy.form.body: Tell us where stock accuracy is hardest today. We will reply with a short slot to confirm the location, category, error band, and approver.
copy.footer.tagline: Stock accuracy, run-out visibility, and cleaner vendor orders for retail and wholesale teams.
copy.footer.privacyNote: Pilot details are used only to review and respond to your request.
copy.form.error: The request did not go through. Please try again.
copy.form.note: Paid four-week pilot · scope and error band agreed before work starts

storeOpsAssumptions.lossRateSource: Wageningen University & Research, supermarket food-loss monitor (2024 data)

storeOpsCopy.lossLabelOne: Food your {stores} store loses to expiry and spoilage
storeOpsCopy.lossLabelOther: Food your {stores} stores lose to expiry and spoilage
storeOpsCopy.lossInfo: Average for Dutch supermarkets: about 1.2% of food bought is lost, mostly to expiry and loss of freshness (Wageningen University & Research, 2024 data). Your own write-offs may be higher or lower.
storeOpsCopy.priceYearly: {amount} a year ({perStore} per store a month)
storeOpsCopy.breakEven: KAI pays for itself if it prevents about {percent} of that loss.
storeOpsCopy.breakEvenOver: At this purchase volume, KAI costs more than the average food loss.
storeOpsCopy.hoursMonthly: About {duration} of ordering work back a month
storeOpsCopy.hoursYearly: About {duration} of ordering work back a year
storeOpsCopy.noTimeSaved: No net time saved at this prep time: review takes about as long as KAI saves.
storeOpsCopy.shareHandledLabel: Share of order preparation KAI handles
storeOpsCopy.reviewMinutesLabel: Review minutes per store per cycle
storeOpsCopy.lossRateLabel: Food lost as a share of purchases
storeOpsCopy.pricePerStoreLabel: KAI price per store per month
storeOpsCopy.hoursFormula: Hours back = stores × cycles per store × (preparation minutes × share KAI handles − review minutes) ÷ 60, rounded.
storeOpsCopy.lossFormula: Food loss = stores × monthly food purchases per store × loss rate, rounded to whole euros.
storeOpsCopy.priceFormula: KAI price = stores × price per store.
storeOpsCopy.breakEvenFormula: Break-even share = KAI price ÷ food loss × 100, rounded.
storeOpsCopy.yearlyNote: The yearly view multiplies hours, food loss and price by 12. The break-even share stays the same.
storeOpsCopy.lossRateNote: The loss rate is measured by weight at participating chains and used here as a share of spend.

copy.methodBody: KAI prepares vendor-ready orders from counts, photos and invoices, and a named approver still reviews each one, so review time is subtracted. The food-loss figure is a published supermarket average shown beside the KAI price for comparison, not a measured or promised saving.
copy.noCurrencyChange: Language changes formatting, not your currency or assumptions.

volume.label: Stores in scope
volume.help: Count locations that would actually run this inventory loop, not every banner in the group.

cycles_per_unit.label: Replenishment cycles per store each month
cycles_per_unit.help: A modelled monthly cadence. Thirteen cycles is about three order cycles per week; replace it with your real cadence.

minutes.label: Preparation minutes per store per cycle
minutes.help: Hands-on count, reconciliation and vendor-order preparation time for one store in one cycle.

purchases_per_store.label: Monthly food purchases per store
purchases_per_store.help: Example figure. Use your own supplier spend.
